title: Timeouts & Retries
description: Separate caller waiting from accepted server work. Compare timeout, queue admission, backoff, seeded jitter and a shared retry budget in a bounded virtual-time model without cancellation or business effects.

presets.title: A timeout leaves server work running
presets.description: A retry adds another accepted unit of work while its timed-out predecessor still runs.

presets.title: Let the healthy response arrive
presets.description: A longer attempt timeout receives the same 80 ms work without a retry.

presets.title: A retry meets a full admission boundary
presets.description: With no waiting room, the retry is rejected while the first accepted work keeps running.

presets.title: Immediate retries spend attempts during an outage
presets.description: Three sends at the same virtual time cannot outwait an unavailable dependency.

presets.title: Backoff can reach a recovered dependency
presets.description: Compare explicit retry delays of 40 and 80 ms with the same authored outage.

presets.title: A proposed retry would miss the deadline
presets.description: Inspect an explicit blocked retry proposal, then the actual overall deadline failure.

presets.title: Planning a retry does not reserve a shared token
presets.description: Two callers plan a retry, but only one can dispatch with the remaining batch budget.

presets.title: Inspect seeded retry delays
presets.description: Replay actual inclusive jitter choices for two callers without assuming spread or success.

assumptions: This illustrative model separates a caller's waiting from accepted server work; it does not model business effects or durable storage.
Authored arrivals and per-request service times determine work; networking and response delivery take zero time.
Attempt timeout begins at send and includes queue wait. Timeout and overall deadline never cancel accepted queued or running work.
Server workers run accepted work to completion in FIFO order; queue capacity excludes running work and idle workers can start with queue capacity zero.
Dependency unavailability and a full waiting queue reject immediately without accepting server work.
Only a response to the currently waiting attempt can succeed its logical request. Late completions cannot revive a caller or satisfy a newer attempt.
Completion wins equality with the overall deadline or attempt timeout; overall deadline wins equality with attempt timeout.
Existing FIFO work is promoted before same-time arrivals, and original sends precede same-time retry sends.
Maximum attempts includes the original. The finite batch retry budget is consumed only by dispatched retries, including immediately rejected ones.
Exponential backoff is capped; FULL jitter draws an inclusive integer delay from one run-local versioned seeded generator.
A proposed retry at or after its arrival-relative overall deadline is not scheduled; the caller waits until that deadline to fail.
All accepted server work drains before the result ends. No-op future timers do not extend the reported final time.
Cancellation, idempotency, actual networking, retry trees, persistence and production latency measurements are excluded.
